To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mobility of Cu is controlled by the interplay of redox and organic matter processes and that Cu mobility is highest in transition areas between oxic and oxygen-free conditions.
Cu mobility along a redox gradient is controlled by (1) the presence of oxygen and the stability of SOM and by (2) the formation of sulfides in anoxic conditions.
the mobility of Cu is strongly controlled by the redox state of the soil, the content and quality of organic matter, the availability of sulfur and the presence of other cations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the behavior of heavy metals in soils and the interplay between different (im)mobilizing processes.
the behavior of Cu along an organic matter and redox gradient, which is relevant for understanding Cu mobility in contaminated soils and in periodically flooded soils, e.g., rice fields.
the behavior of Cu under the influence of redox and organic matter conditions in the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cu mobility is strongly influenced by the interplay of redox and organic matter conditions.
the mobility of Cu in the soil is controlled by a combination of the redox potential, the pH value and the organic matter content.
the mobility of Cu in the studied mofette soil is mainly governed by the presence of organic matter and redox conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cu mobility is controlled by the redox conditions, and the SOM content and quality are the key factors controlling Cu immobilization.
Cu is mobilized in sub-oxic conditions and immobilized in anoxic conditions.
Cu mobility is controlled by redox conditions and SOM, and that the interplay between these two factors determines Cu mobility in the soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cu mobility is not only determined by the redox conditions but also by the stability of organic matter and the presence of sulfide minerals.
Cu mobility is not only dependent on the redox conditions but also on the stability of SOM.
the behavior of Cu under suboxic conditions is highly dependent on the stability of SOM, and thus on the origin of SOM.
